nieuw.titel: Calculate flee paths before choosing charge order
nieuw.tekst: Before declaring and resolving several charges, estimate where fleeing targets could end up. Choose the order with those possible positions in mind, because a fleeing unit may obstruct another charge.
nieuw.waarom: He found that charge order could leave one charger stuck behind a fleeing unit, even though its original lane had been open.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His fleeing Mounted Yeomen landed in the BSB chariot's path towards the Duke. The Boar Boyz redirected into the Mounted Yeomen and destroyed them, opening the chariot's lane again.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He notes that a different flee roll could have carried the Mounted Yeomen through instead, so the outcome was uncertain.

bronnen.citaat: when you're declaring multiple charges, you need to be very careful

nieuw.titel: Prefer a Pegasus mount for the Duke
nieuw.tekst: He considers a Pegasus a far superior mount to a Hippogryph for the Duke, chiefly because of its all-round line of sight.
nieuw.waarom: He points to the Pegasus's 360-degree line of sight, Fly 10 and Swiftstride. He identifies the Hippogryph's Close Order as its main disadvantage in this comparison.

bronnen.citaat: a Pegasus, which would be by far the superior choice.

extraCitaten.citaat: the Pegasus has a 360° line of sight

nieuw.titel: Restrain and reform to preserve several future charge options
nieuw.tekst: After winning with a Close Order hammer, consider restraining and reforming to keep several targets in its charge arc. Anticipate where those targets could move next turn, rather than assuming the nearest target will remain available.
nieuw.waarom: He argues that these units cannot afford turns out of combat. Multiple targets leave alternatives if one moves out of the arc or flees.
nieuw.voorbeeld: After winning with his Duke, he reformed instead of overrunning into Black Orcs, which he expected to be a disastrous fight. He turned towards the Boar Boyz, then later angled to threaten the Doom Diver while keeping options to its right.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says enemy movement cannot always be predicted, so positioning cannot guarantee that a target remains available.

bronnen.citaat: Make a big play out of restraining and reforming.

extraCitaten.citaat: make sure that you are angling in a way that you're still a threat
you need to make sure that you have multiple targets

nieuw.titel: Preserve the champion for a delaying challenge
nieuw.tekst: When using Mounted Knights of the Realm to hold rather than win, keep the champion in the fighting rank so he can challenge an incoming Warboss.
nieuw.waarom: His plan was to keep giving ground or falling back in good order, supported by the battle standard reroll and the nearby Duke's leadership.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He preserved the champion in the fighting rank and challenged the Warboss. The champion died in the first combat, but the unit held through two combats while relying on a reroll on leadership nine.

extraCitaten.citaat: So I could challenge the war boss as it came in

nieuw.titel: Consider fleeing through enemies after their charge declarations
nieuw.tekst: If an escape route runs through another enemy unit, consider fleeing through it after that unit's opportunity to declare charges has passed. Check whether your flee distance is likely to carry you through.
nieuw.waarom: He points out that the other enemy unit could not declare a new charge at the fleeing Knights, even if they had ended inside its charge arc.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His Knights fled from the Warboss through the Black Orcs and escaped their charge arc. He judged that the flee roll plus Swiftstride was likely to clear them.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He had to take a peril test for passing through the Black Orcs and lost two Knights.
